scope_notes: Complete supported denominator generated from pinned server capability/CITE/interop assignments, Esri operation matrices, SDK entrypoints, cloud-native canonical clients, generated gRPC clients, governed external-client assignments for every supported OGC/STAC/SensorThings surface, official MCP SDK/Inspector operations, explicit three-SDK parity cells for every supported protocol and every Honua-specific application capability, executable operation contracts for all three Honua SDKs, explicit fail-closed SDK operation-contract blockers where those contracts do not yet exist, pinned external harnesses for identity, operations, raster, BIM, and point-cloud capabilities, exact operation-to-test contracts for the server protocol integration harness, and one governed test ID per bounded 2026.1 external-client cell. The gRPC scope ruling (grpc-2026.1-implemented-rpcs, geospatial-grpc#88, honua-release#376) keeps 14 RPCs the default honua-server image implements, for 42 generated-client cells. It excludes 66 RPCs (198 cells) as Preview or Experimental, each listed with its rationale and owner issue in sources/geospatial-grpc/operations.v1.json. 5 bounded cells on Preview surfaces are excluded by the preview-surfaces roster ruling and 2 cells no released client can exercise remain non-addressable rows (release#351, release#359). The .NET contract contributes 285 addressable operations; 18 explicitly non-addressable public abstractions remain documented in its pinned source contract and excluded from client certification. Desktop clients are certified against release lines (R38): QGIS 3.44.x and ArcGIS Pro 3.7.x; a receipt records the exact patch it observed. R40 splits those clients by driver. Scripting rows are must-fix-before-cut on every applicable GeoServices and OGC cell. PyQGIS is every server-declared surface crossed with every function that client can perform (connect/discover, add, render, identify, query/filter, edit, raster read, save/reopen, and the auth modes). A function PyQGIS has no client for is not-applicable, and the reason is declared on the row. pro-ui and qgis-ui are must-fix-before-cut only on the core set recorded in the desktop source (FeatureServer, MapServer, ImageServer render, connect, add layer, render, identify, query, FeatureServer edit, and the auth modes; QGIS UI also WMS, WFS, WCS and WFS-T edit). Every other UI cell is prove-against-candidate. Counts per bucket per driver are in desktop_driver_summary. Roadmap Kerchunk and COPC capabilities remain excluded until promoted to supported.

unproduced.missing_producer: integration.yml runs self-contained only on the repository-variable server image; it needs workflow_dispatch inputs that set the self-contained candidate image, server commit and cut (candidate_image, candidate_source_sha, candidate_cut_at) so the nightly can bind it to the resolved candidate.
No producer emits the sdk-coverage entrypoint cells (surface sdk-js:<capability>); protocol-certification-fragment.mjs emits only sdk-js-certification observations.
No producer emits the sdk-coverage entrypoint cells (surface sdk-python:<capability>) or the OGC matrix source-preview cell; conformance.yml emits only sdk-python-certification observations.
No producer emits the sdk-coverage entrypoint cells (surface sdk-dotnet:<capability>); sdk-certification.yml emits only sdk-dotnet-certification observations.
No workflow drives the licensed desktop client UI against a candidate image; esri-sdk-certification.yml runs only the scripting and SDK lanes, so the pro-ui driver cells have no receipt producer.

client-interop-nightly.yml builds its own server image and accepts only a lanes input; it needs candidate_image, candidate_source_sha and candidate_cut_at inputs so its .cert.json receipts name the resolved candidate image digest.
cite-certification.yml maps only versioned surfaces onto a CITE suite; these lanes are cite_lane_status absent in certification/cite-protocol-requirements.v1.json and always emit skips.
No workflow runs the pinned external harnesses (canonical-client-applicability canonical-external-required clients) against a candidate image.

The GDAL/OGR OAPIF driver never requests /conformance: GDAL 3.8.4 and 3.13.3 (the newest release) read only the landing page, the service-desc, /collections and items, even when the landing page links conformance and an attribute filter is set, so GDAL/OGR does not exercise this operation on any server.

The GDAL/OGR OAPIF driver is read-only: in GDAL 3.8.4 and 3.13.3 (the newest release) update-mode open fails, SequentialWrite/RandomWrite/DeleteFeature capabilities are false and CreateFeature returns Unsupported operation even against a server that declares create-replace-delete, so GDAL/OGR does not exercise this operation on any server.
